official_finding.summary: The NTSB determined the probable cause of the San Pedro Bay Pipeline rupture was the proximity of established anchorage positions to the pipeline: on 25 January 2021 a strong cold front drove the containerships MSC DANIT and Beijing to drag anchor, and their anchors struck, displaced (~105 ft) and damaged the pipeline. Undetected, fatigue cracks grew until the pipeline leaked ~9 months later, on 1 October 2021. The volume released was worsened by Beta Offshore's insufficient controller training and failure to shut in the line promptly.

responsible_parties.name: MSC DANIT
responsible_parties.role: anchor strike NTSB names as the initiating event

responsible_parties.name: Beijing
responsible_parties.role: second containership that dragged anchor and contacted the pipeline in the same 25 Jan 2021 storm

responsible_parties.name: Amplify Energy Corp. / Beta Offshore
responsible_parties.role: pipeline operator; delayed shutdown increased the volume released

official_finding.source_name: NTSB Marine Investigation Report MIR-24-01, 'Anchor Strike of Underwater Pipeline and Eventual Crude Oil Release'
official_finding.caveat: The anchor strike preceded the release by eight months -- no vessel was the proximate source at detection time. UDGAM's own infrastructure scorer does not currently name the pipeline: a fixed-source module requires a declared candidate structure and a proximity floor calibrated to the origin cloud's radius, and this case's pipeline candidate falls just under that floor after the age-engine re-run widened the cloud. A dedicated pipeline/oil-well map layer is planned as a separate phase; until it lands, this case is scored purely on transiting vessels, which is the wrong question for it.

udgam_result.origin_summary: Origin cloud centred at 33.5328° N, 118.1443° W; half the ensemble lands within 3.8 km and nine in ten within 7.1 km. Release window 2021-10-01T17:41:51Z to 2021-10-01T19:58:21Z (convergence). Stage 3 funnel 686 → 578 → 7 → 3.

assessment.explanation: UDGAM names three transiting vessels (GOOD JU JU, MORNING CONDUCTOR, WYATT M) at HIGH confidence -- and all three are the wrong answer. The true cause is fixed infrastructure: the San Pedro Bay Pipeline, struck by an anchor eight months before the release NTSB documents. This is stated plainly rather than softened, because the honest reading of the evidence the scorer produced is that it named ships on a case whose source was never a ship. Naming a transiting vessel here is the worst outcome this stage can produce -- a real hull accused of something a federal investigation already attributed elsewhere.
assessment.what_would_have_helped: The infrastructure/pipeline map layer, next phase: a declared candidate structure and a proximity rule that is not silently miscalibrated when the origin cloud's radius changes. Until that lands, this case should be read as 'vessel scoring is the wrong tool here', not as a near-miss on the vessel list.
